title: Chat Integration in 4D v11 SQL
author: Atanas Atanassov, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: EXECUTE ON CLIENT / Execute on Server method property
Blob-based array serialization (VARIABLE TO BLOB / BLOB TO VARIABLE)

historical_commentary.text: This note builds a real-time-feeling chat feature entirely from 4D v11 SQL primitives: a Web Area for rendering, client/server round-trips through EXECUTE ON CLIENT and Execute-on-Server methods, and On Timer polling to simulate push updates, since 4D had no publisher/subscriber or WebSocket mechanism at the time. The polling-and-shared-array architecture is a clever workaround but is inherently laggy and non-scalable compared to what's available now. Modern 4D includes native WebSocket support and server-side push (e.g. session/worker processes, CALL WORKER, and full WebSocket client/server commands added in later v16-v18 releases), which would replace this timer-polling approach entirely, and 4D Write/View Pro-era Web Areas render more modern HTML/JS engines as well.
related_updates: Native WebSocket client/server commands (4D v16 R6+ and later) replace timer-polling for real-time messaging
CALL WORKER / worker processes provide safer inter-process messaging than shared arrays guarded by Execute-on-Server
Modern Web Area engine (Chromium-based, 4D v15+) supersedes the old embedded browser used to render Chat.html
